Along with reporting our third quarter results,

to separate our nutrition business

Abbott entered the nutrition business
more than 60 years ago.

Since that time, we built a strong foundation anchored by a talented global organization,
iconic brands, and established market leadership positions across the pediatric and adult nutrition categories.
The nutrition market has evolved over time, with the pace of change accelerating significantly in recent years.
What was once predominantly viewed as a healthcare market, almost exclusively shaped by healthcare professionals,
has increasingly become a market shape by changing consumer preferences, wellness trends, and retail execution.
While this market evolution is not inherently positive or negative, it has fundamentally changed the environment in which we operate.
So to best position our nutrition business for maximum long-term success, we must evolve and adapt accordingly.
At the same time, Abbott has strategically repositioned its portfolio over the past decade
into attractive, high-growth markets that require sustained investment to drive innovation and support long-term growth.
So we believe both businesses will be better positioned for the future as independent organizations,
each with a distinct identity, reflecting their different customer bases, growth profiles, investment requirements, and innovation cycles.
This separation will enable both companies to sharpen strategic and operational focus,
direct resources more effectively,
and enhance commercial and R&D effectiveness.
As an independent company, nutrition will be uniquely positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for healthy nutrition,
as consumers increasingly recognize the importance of metabolic health
and the role healthy nutrition plays in disease prevention and overall wellness.
The new nutrition company will be created from a position of strength.
The team has done an exceptional job building a balanced growth model supported by sustainable mix,
a volume, and price.
The portfolio includes several iconic brands,
including Similac, PediaSure, Ensure, Glucerna, and Pedialyte,
which have market-leading positions across the pediatric and adult nutrition categories.
With approximately $8.5 billion in annual sales, 16,000 employees, and 14 manufacturing sites,
this will be the largest globally scaled pure-play company in the healthy nutrition market.
Given its scale and financial profile, we would expect this new company to qualify for
inclusion in the S&P 500.

Sales grew 7% in the third quarter, and earnings per share grew 9%,
representing an acceleration.
We saw a significant increase in growth on both top and bottom lines compared to our results
in the first half of the year.
Turning to diagnostics, where sales grew 6.5%, driven by performance
in our core laboratory and cancer diagnostic businesses.
Core lab sales grew 5.5%, driven by strong performance in the U.S.,
Europe, Japan, and Latin America.

and around the world, showed a pattern of strong and stable demand.
We view this as a positive indicator of the underlying demand for healthcare more broadly.
During the third quarter, our testing data continued to support that view,
with testing demand remaining healthy and at durable levels.
In cancer diagnostics, sales growth of 14% was driven by Cologuard and contributions to growth
from our precision oncology and international businesses.
In September, we launched our first blood-based colorectal cancer screening test.
As the only company to offer both stool-based and blood-based screening options,
we are expanding the options available to healthcare providers and patients

Turning to nutrition, sales grew 5%, reflecting broad-based growth across all four categories,
U.S. pediatric, international pediatric, U.S. adult, and international adult.
As I mentioned,
the team has done an exceptional job executing a more balanced growth strategy,
achieving a more sustainable mix of volume and price-driven growth.
In pediatric nutrition, sales grew 9%, led by growth of 11% in the U.S.
As I noted last quarter, the strong performance in the U.S.
includes the benefit from WIC contract wins secured earlier this year,
which helped Abbott regain its market leadership position in both the WIC and non-WIC segments.
In adult nutrition, sales increased 2%, driven by growth of 3.5% in the U.S.
as retail consumption data continues to trend in a positive direction.
We also continue to live strong growth on a sequential basis,
with worldwide nutrition sales increasing more than $100 million compared to the second quarter.
And finally, we continue to make good progress advancing our innovation pipeline.
During the quarter, we launched a new version of our Similac infant formula made with whole milk.
This new product is the first and only commercially sterile, ready-to-feed liquid infant formula made with whole milk available in the United States.
Turning to EPD, where sales increased 8.5% in the quarter.
Our broad portfolio of prescription and over-the-counter medicines, tailored to address local healthcare needs, continues to drive strong growth across emerging markets.

Growth in the quarter was broad-based across geographies and therapeutic areas, and this included double-digit growth in several countries across Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East, highlighting the strong and durable demand that has long been a hallmark of this business.
And I'll wrap up with medical devices, where sales grew 8%.
Growth was well-balanced across the portfolio, led by double-digit growth in electrophysiology and rhythm management.
In electrophysiology, our third quarter results reflected the growth of the medical devices.
Growth in the quarter was mid-teens or high-teens when excluding LAA.
In the U.S., high-teens and exceeded 20% excluding LAA.
This performance was driven by increasing adoption of our new Volt PFA catheter, with momentum accelerating in September, following the transition to a full U.S. market release in mid-August.
International growth also accelerated.
As we continue to capture market share in Europe, driven by increasing uptake of our new PFA catheters and growth in other categories across our broad portfolio.
In September, we received FDA approval earlier than expected for our TactiFlex Duo catheter.
This catheter enables physicians to seamlessly switch between using RF and PFA energy during a procedure.
Given physicians' familiarity with the TactiFlex platform, we expect to execute a broad U.S.
launch starting in the fourth quarter.
In the third quarter, we also received CE mark for our new AMOLED 360 left atrial appendage device, designed to help reduce the risk of stroke in patients with AFib.
We look forward to bringing this new technology to the U.S.
Sales grew 10%, driven by increased adoption of AVERA across both single and dual chamber segments of the pacemaker market.
This expanding use of AVERA is occurring in both the U.S. and international markets.
In diabetes care, continuous glucose monitoring sales grew 8% in the quarter.
In August, we received FDA approval for LibreDuo, the world's first dual glucose ketone bio-variable sensor.
This marks the first time that people with diabetes will be able to monitor ketones without the need for traditional blood or urine tests.
We expect to launch this new sensor in the U.S. in December.
So, in summary, we delivered an acceleration in growth.

On both top and bottom lines, innovation continues to be a key differentiator for Abbott, highlighted by multiple new product approvals and launches that further strengthen our ability to deliver sustainable growth in the years ahead.
And we took an important strategic step towards shaping our future through the planned creation of a new market-leading nutrition company.

Let me begin my remarks with an overview of some of the key aspects of our planning process for the separation.
The first is the separation.
The new nutrition company will become a through a planned, tax-free distribution to Abbott shareholders.

Upon completion of the separation, Abbott shareholders will own shares of both Abbott and the new nutrition company, enabling our shareholders to participate in the value creation opportunities of both businesses.
The final share distribution ratio will be communicated prior to the separation, which we anticipate completing by the end of next year, subject to the required approval.
We incur separation-related costs as we progress through the separation process.
These costs will be treated as specified items and excluded from adjusted earnings.
As a result, we do not expect the separation to have an impact on our supply in January.
We will establish capital structures that ensure both companies have a strong financial foundation.
This includes ensuring adequate capital to support long-term growth objectives and capital allocation priorities, while maintaining strong investment-grade credit ratings for both companies.
As part of that process, we are planning for the new company to raise debt.
With a portion of the project to be completed by the end of next year, we will be able to provide a new financial foundation for Abbott.
We expect a portion of the proceeds to be distributed to Abbott.
The amount of debt to be raised and the amount to be distributed to Abbott will be determined at a later date.
We expect that both Abbott and the new nutrition company will pay a dividend that, when combined, will equal Abbott's dividend at the time of the separation.
Following the separation, we expect Abbott's financial profile to reflect an acceleration in the sales growth and increased profitability.
For the current profile of the nutrition business from the current profile of the Abbott portfolio, we would expect sales growth to accelerate.

We expect the new business to be able to increase sales by 50 to 100 basis points, gross margin as a percent of sales to increase by more than 200 basis points, and an operating margin as a percent of sales to increase by approximately 100 basis points.
On a comparable basis, an adjusted earnings per share of $1.42 was in line with our guidance and the consensus estimate.
Foreign exchange had an unfavorable year-over-year impact of 0.4% on third-quarter sales, which was a slight improvement compared to our expectations at the time of our earnings call in July.
Regarding other aspects of the P&L, the adjusted gross margin profile was 57.2% of sales, representing an increase of 140 basis points compared to the prior year.

The improvement in gross margin was broad-based, reflecting favorable business mix within the legacy Abbott portfolio and from the addition of Exact Sciences, as well as the continued operational improvements and disciplined execution of our margin expansion initiatives.
The adjusted R&D was 6.9% of sales.
And adjusted SG&A was 26.9% of sales.
And based on current rates, we expect exchange to have a negative impact of approximately 1% on fourth-quarters.
